title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GIL FILLS THE GRID
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gil Ramos, a city bus mechanic in San Antonio, Texas.
Every Sunday, Gil starts the newspaper crossword in pen. Every Monday, he peeks at the answers.
His wife Yolanda calls it his weekly surrender.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PEEK
segments.quote: Laziness is nothing more than the habit of resting before you get tired.
segments.author: Jules Renard
lines: One Monday, Yolanda slid a note under his coffee.
It was a line from the French writer Jules Renard:
Laziness is nothing more than the habit of resting before you get tired.
Gil put the answers down. He finished that puzzle on Wednesday, on a bus seat, with grease on his pencil.
Then he entered the library's crossword tournament.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CHAMP
segments.quote: In youth we learn; in age we understand.
segments.author: Marie von Ebner-Eschenbach
lines: The champ: Hazel Dunn, eighty-one, retired court reporter, nine wins straight.
Gil asked her for tips. Young man, she said, I've done this since Eisenhower.
She quoted the Austrian writer Marie von Ebner-Eschenbach:
In youth we learn; in age we understand.
I'm fifty-two, Gil said. Exactly, said Hazel. Tuesdays at four. Bring cookies.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE TRICK
segments.quote: Very few of us are what we seem.
segments.author: Agatha Christie
lines: Gil read clues like a parts manual.
Hazel tapped one: A flower in Paris. Gil wrote tulip. Wrong. Seine. A river. Something that flows.
Hazel quoted Agatha Christie:
Very few of us are what we seem.
Now Gil read every clue twice: once for what it said, once for what it hid.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: BIRD BY BIRD
segments.quote: Bird by bird, buddy. Just take it bird by bird.
segments.author: Anne Lamott
lines: Then came the giant Sunday grid. Gil froze.
Hazel quoted a line from the writer Anne Lamott:
Bird by bird, buddy. Just take it bird by bird.
So Gil did one clue at a time. One at lunch, two before bed.
Yolanda found him asleep with a pencil behind each ear.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LAST SQUARE
segments.quote: When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.
segments.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
lines: Tournament day. Forty people, ticking clocks, and a rattling air conditioner.
One empty square left. Gil had no idea.
He thought of Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes:
When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.
Not A. Not E. Only O fit. He raised his hand two seconds before Hazel.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE NEW CHAMP
segments.quote: Poor is the pupil that does not surpass his master.
segments.author: Leonardo da Vinci
lines: Gil won. He turned to Hazel, ready to apologize.
Hazel stood up clapping and quoted Leonardo da Vinci:
Poor is the pupil that does not surpass his master.
They still meet Tuesdays. Gil brings cookies. Hazel beats him twice a month.
And the Monday answers? Yolanda hid them. Nobody has looked.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Don't peek. Find a teacher. Read twice. Go bird by bird. Rule things out. Cheer your student.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Don't peek. Find a teacher. Read twice. Go bird by bird. Rule things out. Cheer your student.
Me? I still can't finish the word search on a cereal box.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
